Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.
It is informed by learned A.G.A. that opposite party no.2 (complainant) has been served at their end.
2. A report of the concerned police station with regard to the service on opposite party no.2 has been placed before this Court and the same is taken on record.
3. It is also informed that complete/up-to-date case diary has been procured for the assistance of this Court.
Thus, in the considered opinion of this Court, there is sufficient material on the basis of which the plea of bail of the applicant may be adjudicated.

4. Heard Shri Ajay Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the record.

sentences.text: This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Rajan @ Roopchandra for grant of bail, in F.I.R/Case Crime No. 78 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 5/6 P.O.C.S.O. Act, Police Station Gurubux Ganj, District Raebareli, during trial.
6. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.
The F.I.R. of this case was lodged by the father of the prosecutrix/victim on 15.02.2023 alleging therein that the prosecutrix has been enticed away by the applicant on 06.02.2023.
After the recovery of the prosecutrix on 21.02.2023 her statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded.

7. It is vehemently submitted that in the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim had categorically stated to have left her home, as she was scolded by her father and is stated to have gone to the house of her aunt situated at Village Udhakhera, Police Station Maurawan, District Unnao and remained there 10-12 days and denied any relations with the applicant.

However, in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she stated to have accompanied the applicant with her free wish, will and consent and had gone with him to Kanpur and from there to Delhi where they remained for 15 days as husband and wife and also cohabited.

8. It is further submitted that age of the applicant at the relevant point of time was about 18 years and that of the prosecutrix was about 17 years and, thus, the prosecutrix as well as the applicant were not having sufficient intellect to understand the consequences of their act and out of sheer love and affection they decided to fled away in order to solemnize marriage.
However, on being informed that a criminal case has been lodged against them, the prosecutrix/victim had returned herself to her house and has not been recovered from the side of the applicant.
9. It is next submitted that applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 15.03.2023 and he is not having any criminal history.
Charge sheet in this case has already been filed and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
10. Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

11. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that in the first information report, the age of the victim is shown as 17 years and the victim after being recovered in her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has also stated her age to be of 17 years, which is also corroborated by the educational credentials of the prosecutrix.
Thus, it may be taken that the prosecutrix at the relevant point of time was aged about 17 years.
The age of the applicant, as is evident from the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was also about 18 years at the relevant point of time.
Thus, the prosecutrix and the applicant-accused were of very tender age at the relevant point of time.
It is admitted by the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that she had herself accompanied the applicant and they had gone to Delhi where they remained for 15 days.

Thus, the prosecutrix evidently was a consenting party and in the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. by the investigating officer, the Rajan @ Roopchandra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ...

Thus, having regard to the tender age of both, accused applicant and the prosecutrix/victim and the admission of the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., in the considered opinion of this Court, is sufficient to exercise discretion in favour of the applicant, moreso the applicant is in jail in this case since 15.03.2023 without any criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in this case has also been filed and the presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

12. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

13. Let the accused/applicant- Rajan @ Roopchandra involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
15. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
16. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
